title: A browser-gated turn past the spend ceiling waits silently instead of being refused
description:
Found in the live run of chatticus-1d68fb (dev, 2026-09-19).

Repro: org anthus with ceiling 100 and today's ok rollup row at 150 (GET /me correctly reports status=enabled, computer_work_paused=true, reason 'monthly AWS spend ceiling exceeded'). Ask ExerciseBot-0b7a36c3 'Open the household browser and tell me the title of example.com'.

Observed: the bot streams a draft, the worker parks the turn via POST /turns/{id}/waiting (gate=browser). No ceiling check on that path: control_plane.emit_turn_waiting and the wait_turn route in http/app.py never call _refuse_if_computer_work_paused; enforcement exists only in prepare_computer_tool and request_computer_host_start, which this path did not reach. Turn 579633e0-ca09-4475-9d92-119afe7e5bd2 stayed status=active, waiting_for=browser, past its deadline (13:00:43Z), with no continuation queued and no ECS task started. The thread showed 'Waiting for the bot to finish responding' and the composer stayed blocked.

Good: fail-closed (no computer started), org stayed enabled. Bad: no refusal, no reason in the thread, no terminal event, member cannot send in that thread. Fix: refuse (denied tool result, complete the turn) at the waiting gate when paused, mirroring the host-start denial in 6a9e97, with Gherkin driving the /waiting path. Also decide what ends an active turn parked past its deadline.
